description: Nextcloud service health: the exporter's own metrics plus the Traefik, CNPG, volume and CronJob signals that actually explain an outage.

panels.title: Nextcloud API
panels.description: nextcloud_up from the exporter: 1 means the serverinfo API answered. This is the single signal that says Nextcloud itself is alive, as opposed to Traefik merely routing to it.

panels.title: Server errors (5xx)
panels.description: Share of requests Traefik answered with 5xx. Sustained non-zero here is a real fault; brief blips happen during rolling restarts.

panels.title: Throttled (429)/s
panels.description: Nextcloud's bruteforce throttle. A shared source IP (e.g. all tunnel traffic arriving as one cloudflared pod IP) makes this spike for everyone at once.

panels.title: Failing maintenance jobs
panels.description: Failed Job objects still present in the namespace. These are kept by history limits, so a non-zero count can be old news - check the Maintenance jobs row for which cronjob is actually behind.

panels.title: Requests by status class
panels.description: Grouped by class rather than by code - the raw code breakdown is 20+ series, which is unreadable. Drill into 4xx below.

panels.title: Client errors by code (4xx)
panels.description: 401 = Authelia challenge (normal). 423 = locked file. 429 = bruteforce throttle. 404 at volume usually means a client hammering a path that no longer exists.

panels.title: Rate limiting and server errors
panels.description: 499 means the client disconnected before Nextcloud answered - with a ~100s tunnel timeout in front, a rise here points at slow requests rather than errors.

panels.title: Active now
panels.description: Users seen in the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Free space reported by Nextcloud
panels.description: What Nextcloud itself believes is free on its data directory. Compare against the per-volume numbers: they disagree when the data dir is not the volume that is actually filling up.

panels.title: Free space per volume
panels.description: max by claim, because RWX volumes are reported once per mounting node and would otherwise show up three times.

panels.title: Last backup age
panels.description: Age of the newest available base backup. Backups to storage01 have been paused before; this is the panel that would have made that visible.

panels.title: WAL waiting to archive
panels.description: Segments in .ready state. A climbing number means archiving is broken and the data volume will fill - this is also what blocks a demoted primary from rejoining.

panels.title: Collector errors
panels.description: Errors from the CNPG metrics collector itself. Non-zero here means the numbers on this row may be stale, so read it before trusting the rest.

panels.title: Container restarts
panels.description: Cumulative, not a rate - a step up is a restart.

panels.title: Time since last successful run
panels.description: nextcloud-cron running late is the usual cause of stuck background jobs (previews, file scans, notifications).

panels.title: Failed jobs still present
panels.description: One row per failed Job object. Cross-check the timestamp in the job name against the age column on the left before treating it as a live problem.

panels.title: Max upload size
panels.description: php upload_max_filesize. Large-file uploads that fail at a consistent size are hitting this, not a storage problem.

panels.title: Exporter scrape errors
panels.description: When this is non-zero every nextcloud_* panel above is running on stale data.
